name: Git and Teamwork: Version Control, Review and Process
summary: Version your code, never lose work again — and learn how a team actually moves a task: the board, the ticket, the review and what "done" means to somebody else.
prerequisites: No programming required: version control comes before the first language, and so does knowing how a team moves a task from an idea to production.
syllabus: GitHub and GitLab: remotes, pull requests and code review
How a team works: board, ticket, review and the definition of done
Good practice for messages and organisation
topics: What version control is and why it exists
History: log, diff, blame and show
Undoing safely: restore, revert and reset
Branches: create, switch, merge and delete
Remotes: clone, fetch, pull, push and tags
GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket: issues, pull requests and code review
Workflows: feature branch, trunk based and Git Flow
Commit messages and the Conventional Commits standard
The life of a task: ticket, branch, pull request, review, merge, release
Reviewing somebody else’s code: what to comment on and what to let go
Receiving a review without taking it personally
Sprint, kanban and the board: the vocabulary of the week
Refinement, estimation, and the ticket that was not ready to start
Definition of done, and what "it works on my machine" costs the team
Stand-up, planning and retrospective: the meetings, and what they are for
Working alongside product, design and QA without being surprised at the end
